page: Microsoft Azure L2ps_v5 is an arm64 virtual machine instance within Azure's storage-optimized Lpsv5 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Hardware acceleration is not present on this tier, which features zero GPU units.

Storage capabilities include a bundled 480 GB local NVMe solid-state drive that provides low-latency direct-attached storage for temporary caching, indexing, or scratch space. In addition to the local NVMe media, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud virtual network routing for outbound or inbound access.

The hardware configuration couples energy-efficient 64-bit Arm computing cores with a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe block storage. This profile yields high resource efficiency for workloads that demand substantial memory headroom and high-throughput disk access per compute core. The server fits database engines, NoSQL repositories, log aggregation agents, search index nodes, and distributed cache layers requiring fast local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure L2ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes a direct-attached 480 GB NVMe solid-state drive for low-latency local disk operations alongside Premium Storage support. It contains no GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The pairing of Arm processing with integrated NVMe media delivers dense storage I/O and memory capacity in a compact core configuration without unnecessary compute overhead. Given its balance of dedicated Arm cores, high memory-to-vCPU ratio, and fast local NVMe storage, this server is suitable for intermediate database engines, NoSQL key-value stores, distributed logging nodes, and read-heavy caching systems requiring fast local scratch or working space.
